newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to cut government securities issue in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia to cut government securities issue in 1997.

text.p: Russia's 1997 draft budget provides for a fall in the issue of government securities to 49.70 trillion roubles ($9.1 billion) from 56.66 trillion budgeted for 1996, figures supplied by the Finance Ministry to the conciliation commission examining the draft say.
The issue of GKO discount Treasury bills will fall to 15.00 trillion roubles in 1997 from 22.22 trillion in 1996, according to the figures, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
The issue of OFZ interest-bearing government bonds will fall to 30.70 trillion roubles in 1996 from 32.44 trillion in 1996, it says.
Officials have said they want to switch the burden of borrowing on to longer-term paper.
Total domestic funding of the 90.70 trillion rouble deficit will fall to 49.48 trillion in 1997 from 56.10 trillion roubles in 1996.
The difference between total domestic funding and securities issues reflects repayments of central bank credits.
The draft also proposes issuing one trillion roubles of gold-backed bonds after a budgeted two trillion roubles in 1996. The gold bonds have not been issued so far.
The issue of savings bonds will fall to three trillion roubles in 1997 from four trillion roubles in 1996, it says.
Foreign borrowing to cover the deficit will rise to 41.22 trillion from 32.45 trillion roubles, it said.
The biggest rise will take place in borrowing from international commercial banks and firms, rising to 7.24 trillion roubles from 1.65 trillion in 1996.
Russia has announced it plans to issue several hundred millions of dollars of Eurobonds next year, with a debut issue at the end of this year.

Credits from international finance organisations, including the disbursements under the $10 billion three-year loan from the International Monetary Fund, will fall to 24.90 trillion roubles in 1997 from 25.00 trillion roubles in 1996. ($1=5458 Rouble)
